transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-09
Time: 4:00 PM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood CSM)


Mike Reynolds (CTO, Summit), Sara Gomez (Security Lead), Elena Park (Eng Manager), James Holt (Infra)

Summary (auto gen): initial security posture discovery to evaluate Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for Summit Biotech POC. Discussion covered SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data retention, and BYOK/HSM requirements. Action items and next steps captured.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh quick intros, I'll kick off 
[00:12] Mike Reynolds: hi Alex, Mike here, CTO at Summit. we've been evaluating a few inference options, security is the gating factor.
[00:20] Sara Gomez: Sara, security lead. main concerns: data residency, BYOK, audit logs, and how long logs/inputs are retained.
[00:28] Alex Chen: makes sense. Priya, do you want to jump into the high level on compliance and options?
[00:33] Priya Patel: sure. thanks. Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC or on-prem). hosted is fastest to get started and is SOC2 Type II compliant, ISO 27001 org-wide as well 
[01:05] Elena Park: can you clarify the differences for key management 
[01:10] Priya Patel: yes. for Dedicated we offer BYOK via KMS integration 
[01:34] Sara Gomez: and do you have separation between metadata and payload? i.e., are prompts ever stored unencrypted for analytics?
[01:41] Priya Patel: by default, input prompts are not used for training; we have retention policies. on hosted the default logs retention is 90 days for request/response logs but you can opt-in to longer retention or request no retention; for Dedicated/Private you control retention via configuration, and logs can be sent to your SIEM via forwarders.
[02:05] James Holt: what about audit logs and RBAC 
[02:12] Alex Chen: good point. Redwood Console supports RBAC with roles (admin, ops, viewer), SSO via SAML/Okta, and we surface audit logs for admin events, model deploys, rollouts, and key access. audit logs are append-only and can be exported to customer logging like Splunk or CloudWatch.
[02:32] Priya Patel: to add, our audit events include per-request metadata (no raw prompt in audit by default unless configured), model version, user identity, route, latency, and token counts. customers can configure redaction rules for pii.
[02:46] Sara Gomez: can you sign an SLA that covers data handling? and do you have documented procedures for key rotation and incident response?
[02:54] Alex Chen: yes, for enterprise we offer SLAs in Dedicated/Private contracts and have documented key rotation and IR playbooks. we'll include the IR summary and key lifecycle doc in the follow-up.
[03:06] Mike Reynolds: another ask 
[03:13] Alex Chen: absolutely. we'll share SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 cert, plus high level vulnerability testing summaries and scope.
[03:21] Elena Park: what about network isolation? we run workloads in a hybrid environment, want egress restrictions and enforced private connectivity.
[03:29] Priya Patel: for Dedicated we can do VPC peering with restricted egress, and Private supports on-prem installation behind your firewall. For hosted we also provide private endpoints and region controls but it's not the same as fully air-gapped on-prem.
[03:46] James Holt: any specifics on encryption in transit? TLS only or mTLS?
[03:50] Priya Patel: TLS 1.2/1.3 for all traffic, and mutual TLS (mTLS) is supported for Private and can be configured for Dedicated.
[03:58] Sara Gomez: about SSO 
[04:06] Alex Chen: yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; 2FA enforcement is configurable at the IdP level. we'll send the SAML metadata and a quickstart guide.
[04:16] Mike Reynolds: latency/cost tradeoffs 
[04:22] Priya Patel: Dedicated actually reduces compliance work on your side because it's still Redwood-managed infra but with isolation. Private (on-prem) shifts more operational responsibility to you. We can walk though which controls remain Redwood responsibility vs customer in a RACI for the pilot.
[04:39] Elena Park: we need to run a benchmark with our sample prompts. can Redwood run a loading test and provide token-level latency breakdowns?
[04:46] Priya Patel: yes, we can do a POC benchmark on Dedicated with your prompts. we'll also provide per-token latency and cost breakdowns and recommendations like batching/kv cache settings.
[04:58] Sara Gomez: retention policy question 
[05:07] Alex Chen: we support separate retention windows. by default request/response retention is 90 days, audit logs 365 days, but for enterprise we offer extended log retention and archival to your storage for 7+ years. we can configure redaction/retention to meet PII regulations.
[05:24] James Holt: and for legal/procurement 
[05:31] Alex Chen: yes, we support region pinning for hosted and Dedicated. Private obviously runs in your region. we'll share our region availability matrix.
[05:38] Mike Reynolds: curious about model variants and fallback 
[05:46] Priya Patel: rollout events are logged in audit. we support canary deploys and automatic fallbacks, and all of those rollout decisions and who initiated them are recorded in the audit log.
[05:58] Elena Park: who owns the KV cache and what is stored there? could sensitive tokens be cached?
[06:04] Priya Patel: KV cache is ephemeral and in-memory by default; sensitive material is not persisted. for strict environments we can disable caching or ensure caches are per-tenant and encrypted. we'll document cache behavior for the POC.
[06:18] Sara Gomez: what about legal requests / subpoena handling? we need to know how Redwood responds.
[06:24] Alex Chen: we have a legal process for requests and will notify customers per contract. for Dedicated/Private customers, the contract can specify notice periods and handling. we'll include our law enforcement request policy.
[06:36] Mike Reynolds: ok good. next steps from Summit perspective: we'd like the SOC2 docs, the SAML metadata, the security questionnaire answers, and then schedule the infra deep-dive next week.
[06:48] Alex Chen: great. Priya, Daniel and I will follow up 
[07:03] Sara Gomez: one more note 
[07:12] Alex Chen: yes we can coordinate that. we typically support VAPT engagements on enterprise pilots 
[07:20] Mike Reynolds: timeline 
[07:24] Alex Chen: sounds reasonable. we'll aim to have the security packet and scheduling details in 2-3 business days and the technical deep-dive by next week.
[07:32] Daniel Ortiz: I'll own the contract kickoff and procurement questions; I'll also add a short checklist for data residency and retention options.
[07:38] Elena Park: thanks, that's helpful.
[07:41] Alex Chen: ok wrapping up 
[07:49] Mike Reynolds: thanks everyone. looking forward to the follow-up.

End of transcript.
